relevance_note: Supplementary Table S2 gives genotype, onset, sex and clinical data per patient for the HA20 subgroup: 'nine patients (from six unrelated families) in the study were diagnosed with HA20'.
method_note: Read the whole paper including the converted supplement. Individual-level data for the in-scope people exist only in Table S2 ('Genotypes and clinical phenotypes of patients with A 20 haploinsufficiency', supplementary DataSheet_1.pdf), a preformatted text table in which each patient record wraps over two or three lines; cells on continuation lines are quoted as extra spans beside the row segment that starts with the patient number. A Python script assembled the JSON; every value was chosen by my reading, and spans were sliced from the paper's lines and then checked verbatim. Labels 'Patient 1'..'Patient 9' are the Table S2 'Patient' column numbers (footnote marker 'a' on 5a/6a/7a dropped; the footnote itself uses 'patient 5', 'Patients 6 and 7'); they are NOT the Table 2 numbering (Table 2 patients 1-19 are undiagnosed patients without TNFAIP3 variants, e.g. Patient 1 with PSMB8 variants, and are out of scope). Figure S1 heatmap rows HA20-1..HA20-9 (two printed 'HS20-2', 'HS20-9') are probably the same patients but the paper does not link them, so they were not used. Table S2 columns used: 'Gender', 'Age at IS analysis' (recorded as age at last evaluation; it is the age at blood sampling), 'Disease-onset age', 'genotype', 'Initial diagnosis before genetic analysis', 'Symptoms at IS analysis', 'Treatment at IS analysis'. Entries of the initial-diagnosis column (e.g. SLE, Crohn's disease, Hashimoto's disease, pJIA, intestinal BD) were recorded as observed features with that qualifier. Abbreviations pJIA, sJIA, BD and RF are not defined in the paper and were read as standard medical abbreviations (pJIA/sJIA counted as arthritis; intestinal BD and Crohn's disease counted as gastrointestinal inflammation). 'Stomatitis' was not counted as oral ulcers. CRP at IS analysis (mg/L) values (7, 5, <0.2, 7.1, 0.8, 11.3; N/D for patients 1, 2, 7) were not recorded as features because the paper gives no reference range; 'None' under 'Symptoms at IS analysis' was not used to exclude any feature (it describes one time point). Inheritance left 'not reported' for all (patient 5's mother and grandmother carry the same variant, but the paper does not state inheritance). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = true refers ONLY to out-of-scope Table 2 patients 7 and 11 (footnote c, refs 34, 35); for the HA20 patients the paper cites ref (32) only for 'previously reported variants', not patients. Out of scope (no rows): the other 85 of the 94 patients (undiagnosed Table 2 patients, IPH, CAEBV, HMB and other disease groups) and the 23 controls. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) 'nine patients (from six unrelated families)' but the only stated relationship is patients 5, 6, 7 (mother and grandmother of 5), which would give seven families; no further relationship is stated, so no family labels were assigned (patients 2 and 4 share c.133C>T, p.Arg45* but are not stated to be related). (2) Abstract: '117 samples from 94 patients'; Methods: 'Samples were collected from a total of 117 individuals' (57 + 37 patients plus controls) and 'IFN signatures were measured in 140 samples'; cohort_size_as_stated uses 94 patients. (3) Results call p.Lys329Asn*1 and p.Gly583* 'newly confirmed to be pathogenic', while the Discussion mentions 'variants of unknown significance are found in the TNFAIP3 gene, as in the present study'.
